explanation: The can is made of metal (tin/steel) with a paper label covering most of the body. The top lid is bare metal with a slightly matte finish showing concentric ridges. The metallic rims at top and bottom have a moderate metallic sheen. The paper label is non-metallic with a slightly glossy printed surface. Overall, the material is a mix of metal and paper, so the metallic value should be moderate (leaning toward the metal components visible at top and rim), and the roughness should be moderate as the metal surfaces show some wear and the paper label has a semi-glossy finish.
